properties.name: Pegunungan Barisan (Bukit Barisan Mountain System)
properties.description: ~1,700 km long spine mountain system of Sumatra, formed by Cenozoic magmatic arc activity and oblique plate convergence along the Sunda-Java trench.
properties.rock_type: Granitoid batholiths, andesite-dacite volcanics, pre-Tertiary metamorphic basement
properties.evidence_description: Continuous high-relief fault-bounded mountain belt traversing Sumatra with dissected volcanic massifs and pull-apart basins along the Great Sumatran Fault.
properties.evidence_significance: Represents the primary morphotectonic backbone of Sumatra, illustrating magmatic arc evolution and strike-slip terrane deformation.
properties.why_it_matters: The Barisan Mountains host major active geothermal systems, mineralized plutonic complexes, and active tectonic fault grabens across Sumatra.
properties.source: Barber, A.J., Crow, M.J. & Milsom, J.S. (eds.) (2005) Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution, Geological Society of London Memoir 31, 290 p.; Van Bemmelen, R.W. (1949) The Geology of Indonesia.

properties.name: Pegunungan Meratus (Meratus Suture & Ophiolite Complex)
properties.description: Uplifted Cretaceous subduction-accretion complex and ophiolitic suture belt in South Kalimantan, separating the Barito and Asem-Asem basins.
properties.rock_type: Serpentinized peridotite, gabbro, pillow basalt, radiolarian chert, schist
properties.evidence_description: Exposed Mesozoic ultramafic ophiolite sequence and high-pressure blueschist metamorphic blocks thrust over continental basement.
properties.evidence_significance: Crucial suture zone marking Cretaceous collision between the Schwaner/Sundaland block and East Java-Paternoster microcontinent.
properties.why_it_matters: Exposes Earth mantle rocks and paleo-subduction mélange in Kalimantan, fundamental for SE Asian paleogeographic reconstructions.
properties.source: Wakita, K., Miyazaki, K., Zulkarnain, I., Sopaheluwakan, J., & Sanyoto, P. (1998) 'Tectonic implications of new age data for the Meratus Complex of south Kalimantan, Indonesia', The Island Arc, 7(1–2): 202–222; Sikumbang (1986).

properties.name: Pegunungan Selatan Jawa (Southern Mountains Zone)
properties.description: Classic physiographic zone of Java established by Van Bemmelen (1949), comprising Oligo-Miocene volcanic arc formations (OAF) overlain by Miocene limestones.
properties.rock_type: Old Andesite Formation (OAF) breccia, dacitic tuff, Wonosari limestone
properties.evidence_description: Continuous uplifted plateau and rugged coastal ranges forming the southern structural flank of Java.
properties.evidence_significance: Preserves the ancient Paleogene volcanic arc before the subduction zone migrated to its modern Quaternary volcanic axis.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides key stratigraphical record of the transition from ancient volcanic arc activity to extensive carbonate platform deposition.
properties.location_province: Jawa (Jawa Barat, DIY, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur)
properties.source: Smyth, H.R., Hall, R., & Nichols, G.J. (2008) 'Cenozoic volcanic arc history of East Java, Indonesia', Geological Society of London Special Publications, 311: 199–222; Van Bemmelen, R.W. (1949).

properties.name: Pegunungan Kendeng (Kendeng Fold-Thrust Belt)
properties.description: East-west trending fold-and-thrust belt in Central-East Java, formed by intense Plio-Pleistocene compression of a deep marine volcaniclastic trough.
properties.rock_type: Turbiditic sandstone, marl, volcaniclastic flysch (Kerek, Kalibeng, Pucangan formations)
properties.evidence_description: Series of asymmetric anticlines, synclines, and south-verging blind thrust faults (Kendeng Thrust).
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates active crustal shortening and sedimentary basin inversion within the back-arc realm of Java.
properties.why_it_matters: The Kendeng Zone hosts significant onshore petroleum potential and active blind thrust seismic hazard sources in Java.
properties.source: de Genevraye, P., & Samuel, L. (1972) 'Geology of the Kendeng Zone (Central & East Java)', Proceedings Indonesian Petroleum Association (IPA) 1st Annual Convention, pp. 17–30; Van Bemmelen, R.W. (1949).

properties.name: Pegunungan Maoke (Central Range of Papua)
properties.description: Parent Central Cordillera of Papua spanning ~1,300 km, formed by Neogene collision between the Indo-Australian passive margin and Pacific-Caroline oceanic arcs.
properties.rock_type: Mesozoic-Cenozoic limestone, metamorphic phyllite, porphyry intrusive complexes
properties.evidence_description: Massive alpine fold-thrust mountain belt exceeding 4,800 m elevation with remnant tropical glaciers on Puncak Jaya.
properties.evidence_significance: Prime example of active continent-arc collision orogeny producing highest topography in Australasia and giant porphyry Cu-Au deposits.
properties.why_it_matters: Contains Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid, 4,884 m) and preserves crucial tectonic records of Australian northern margin collision.
properties.source: Cloos, M., Sapiie, B., Quarles van Ufford, A., Weiland, R.J., Warren, P.Q., & McMahon, T.P. (2005) Collisional delamination in New Guinea: The geotectonics of subducting slab breakoff, Geological Society of America Special Paper 400; Dow et al. (1988).

properties.name: Cekungan Bandung (Bandung Volcano-Tectonic Basin)
properties.description: Quaternary volcano-tectonic intermontane depression surrounded by volcanic edifices and bounded north by Sesar Lembang, site of ancient Lake Bandung.
properties.rock_type: Lacustrine clay, tuffaceous sand, volcanic breccia, peat
properties.evidence_description: Flat basin floor (~650-700 m ASL) surrounded by steep volcanic massifs with well-documented lacustrine terrace deposits.
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates volcano-tectonic basin subsidence, ancient lake damming (Danau Purba Bandung), and ongoing intra-arc tectonic deformation.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides paleoenvironmental archive of prehistoric Java and critical geological context for seismic and hydrogeological risk in Bandung Raya.
properties.source: Dam, M.A.C., Suparan, P., Nossin, J.J., & Voskuil, R.P.G.A. (1996) 'A chronology for geomorphological developments in the greater Bandung area, West-Java, Indonesia', Journal of Southeast Asian Earth Sciences, 14(1–2): 101–115.

properties.name: Cekungan Barito (Barito Sedimentary Basin)
properties.description: Asymmetric Tertiary sedimentary basin in South Kalimantan bounded east by the Meratus thrust front and west by the stable Sunda Shield.
properties.rock_type: Tanjung Formation sandstone/shale, Berai limestone, Warukin coal-bearing sandstone
properties.evidence_description: Thick transgressive-regressive sedimentary sequence (up to 6,000 m) with foreland flexural geometry adjacent to Meratus.
properties.evidence_significance: Classic Indonesian hydrocarbon and coal-bearing sedimentary basin illustrating back-arc rift to foreland basin transition.
properties.why_it_matters: One of Indonesia's most thoroughly studied sedimentary basins, hosting significant energy resources and thick coal seams.
properties.source: Witts, D., Hall, R., Nichols, G., & Morley, R.J. (2012) 'A new depositional and provenance model for the Tanjung Formation, Barito Basin, SE Kalimantan, Indonesia', Journal of Asian Earth Sciences, 56: 77–104.

properties.name: Karst Gunung Sewu (Gunung Sewu UNESCO Global Geopark)
properties.description: World-benchmark tropical cone karst (kegelkarst) and cockpit karst developed in Middle-Late Miocene Wonosari Formation limestones.
properties.rock_type: Wonosari Formation coral limestone, calcarenite, speleothems
properties.evidence_description: Over 40,000 conical limestone hills, thousands of sinkholes (doline/uvala), and extensive subterranean river networks and caves (Luweng Ombo, Luweng Jaran).
properties.evidence_significance: International type-locality for tropical conical karst geomorphology and Quaternary hominin habitation caves (Song Terus).
properties.why_it_matters: Designated a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2015, Gunung Sewu is a global benchmark for tropical speleology, hydrogeology, and geoheritage.
properties.source: Haryono, E., & Day, M. (2004) 'Landform differentiation within the Gunung Kidul Kegelkarst, Java, Indonesia', Journal of Cave and Karst Studies, 66(2): 62–69; UNESCO Global Geoparks Network Dossier (2015).

properties.name: Palung Sunda-Jawa (Sunda-Java Subduction Trench)
properties.description: ~3,000 km oceanic subduction trench (depth 6,000-7,450 m) where the Indo-Australian oceanic plate subducts beneath the Sundaland continental plate.
properties.rock_type: Oceanic basalt, pelagic sediment, accretionary prism wedge
properties.evidence_description: Deep bathymetric V-shaped trough (>7,000 m), dipping Wadati-Benioff seismic zone, and accretionary forearc ridges (Mentawai, Enggano).
properties.evidence_significance: Primary convergent megathrust generating Indonesia's active volcanism, island arc uplift, and megathrust earthquakes/tsunamis.
properties.why_it_matters: The Sunda-Java Trench is one of Earth's most active convergent margins, driving regional plate tectonics and geohazards.
properties.location_province: Offshore Indian Ocean (Sumatra, Java, Bali, Nusa Tenggara)

properties.name: Busur Vulkanik Sunda (Sunda Volcanic Arc Front Axis)
properties.description: Curvilinear chain of active Quaternary stratovolcanoes and magmatic arc complexes spanning Sumatra, Java, Bali, Lombok, Sumbawa, and Flores.
properties.rock_type: Calc-alkaline andesite, basaltic andesite, dacite, pyroclastic deposits
properties.evidence_description: Chain of over 100 active Quaternary volcanic centers positioned ~100-200 km above the subducting Indo-Australian slab.
properties.evidence_significance: Illustrates active subduction-induced mantle melting, crustal magma differentiation, and stratovolcano construction along Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Forms the volcanic backbone of Western Indonesia, generating fertile soils, geothermal energy, and active volcanic hazards.

properties.name: Sesar Lembang (Active Fault Trace)
properties.description: Active sinistral strike-slip fault with normal component extending ~29 km north of Bandung.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent north-facing fault scarp, stream offsets, and paleoseismic trenching evidence.
properties.evidence_significance: Slip rate ~3-6 mm/yr capable of generating M6.5-7.0 seismic events near Bandung metropolitan area.
properties.why_it_matters: Key active onshore fault in West Java with well-documented morphotectonic fault scarps.

properties.name: Sesar Cimandiri (Fault Zone)
properties.description: Major active oblique strike-slip fault zone extending from Pelabuhanratu Bay through Sukabumi to Padalarang.
properties.evidence_description: Morphotectonic valley linear, offset river terraces, and shallow crustal seismicity.
properties.evidence_significance: Major morphotectonic boundary separating northern Java fold belt from southern volcanic arc terrane.
properties.why_it_matters: Active fault zone responsible for periodic destructive shallow earthquakes in West Java.

properties.name: Sesar Baribis (Thrust Belt Zone)
properties.description: Major back-arc thrust fault system in West-Central Java accommodating crustal shortening.
properties.evidence_description: North-verging thrust ramps, asymmetric folding, and GPS geodetic strain accumulation.
properties.evidence_significance: Accommodates back-arc shortening across Java with geodetic locking along southern Jakarta-Bogor corridor.
properties.why_it_matters: Critical active tectonic structure representing back-arc seismic hazard in northern Java.

properties.description: Active strike-slip fault zone along Opak river graben, source zone of 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake.
properties.rock_type: Alluvium, Merapi volcanic ash, Tertiary limestone basement
properties.evidence_description: Linear morphotectonic graben boundary and persistent shallow micro-seismicity.
properties.evidence_significance: Active crustal fault controlling intra-arc basin development and seismic hazard in Yogyakarta.
properties.why_it_matters: Site of the devastating 2006 Mw 6.3 Yogyakarta earthquake.

properties.description: Southernmost segment of Great Sumatran Fault entering Semangko Bay, accommodating oblique convergence.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent graben valley, strike-slip fault scarps, and geothermal spring alignments.
properties.evidence_significance: Key dextral strike-slip transform accommodating partitioned oblique subduction shear along Sumatra.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates trench-parallel slip partitioning in oblique convergent margins.

properties.name: Sesar Sorong (Fault System)
properties.description: Major left-lateral transform fault zone in Eastern Indonesia, accommodating Pacific-Australian plate motion.
properties.evidence_description: Transpressional ridges, pull-apart basins, and displaced continental fragments.
properties.evidence_significance: Key strike-slip structure transporting continental fragments from Australia/PNG westward into the Banda arc region.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates rapid strike-slip terrane transport shaping Eastern Indonesia's complex tectonic mosaic.

properties.name: Kompleks Melange Ciletuh (Subduction Complex)
properties.description: Pre-Tertiary subduction melange complex exposed at Ciletuh, West Java, featuring chaotic blocks of ophiolite, metamorphic schists, and deep-marine sediments.
properties.evidence_description: Exposed tectonic mélange blocks comprising oceanic crustal rocks embedded in sheared matrix.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides direct petrological evidence of ancient Cretaceous subduction accretion along Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Ciletuh exposes Java's oldest basement rocks, allowing geoscientists to reconstruct Cretaceous plate subduction history.

properties.description: Cretaceous subduction accretionary complex exposing ophiolite sequence, pillow basalts, red chert, and tectonic melange in Kebumen, Central Java.
properties.rock_type: Pillow Basalt, Red Chert, Serpentinite, Mica Schist
properties.evidence_description: Deep marine pillow basalts and radiolarian chert blocks structurally chaotic in scaly clay matrix.
properties.evidence_significance: Classic Indonesian tectonic benchmark site illustrating ancient subduction zone lithologies.

properties.name: Ngandong Homo erectus (Solo Man) Site
properties.description: Late Pleistocene alluvial terrace locality along the Bengawan Solo River where 14 Homo erectus (Solo Man) calvaria and tibia were discovered between 1931 and 1933.
properties.discovery_locality: Bengawan Solo High Terrace, Ngandong, Blora
properties.fossil_material: 14 cranial calvaria, tibia fragments, Stegodon & Bubalus fossils
properties.paleoenvironment: Open-woodland riverine terrace and seasonal floodplain
properties.evidence_description: Fossilized cranial and tibial remains of Homo erectus discovered within stratified terrace sand and gravel beds of the High Terrace of Bengawan Solo.
properties.evidence_significance: Stratified cranial elements confirm the survival of late Homo erectus in Java until the late Middle-to-Late Pleistocene transition.
properties.why_it_matters: Ngandong represents the youngest globally documented population of Homo erectus, providing critical chronological constraints on hominin survival in Southeast Asia.

properties.description: Early Pleistocene volcanic-alluvial site in Jetis, Mojokerto, famous for the 1936 discovery of the juvenile Pithecanthropus mojokertensis (Mojokerto child) skull.

properties.evidence_significance: Provides direct fossil evidence for the earliest hominin colonization of Sundaland during the Early Pleistocene.
properties.why_it_matters: One of the oldest hominin specimens in Southeast Asia (~1.8 Ma), demonstrating early hominin adaptability across tropical volcanic delta environments.

properties.name: Sambungmacan Progressive Homo erectus Site

properties.name: Molucca Sea Double Subduction Collision Zone
properties.geological_process: Opposing double-vergent subduction of the Molucca Sea Plate beneath both the Sangihe Arc (west) and Halmahera Arc (east), with the central Talaud-Mayu Ridge forming an uplifted ophiolitic and melange collision complex.
properties.description: The Molucca Sea Collision Zone is the world's premier modern active example of an arc-arc collision driven by opposing double subduction. The Molucca Sea Plate is an inverted U-shaped oceanic slab being consumed simultaneously to the west beneath the Sangihe Arc and to the east beneath the Halmahera Arc. The central collision complex is exposed at the Talaud, Mayu, and Tifore islands.
properties.discovery_locality: Molucca Sea (Talaud-Mayu Ridge, Mayu & Tifore Islands)
properties.geometry_note: Representative regional boundary polygon enclosing the Molucca Sea collision complex and Talaud-Mayu deformation zone between the opposing Sangihe and Halmahera forearcs, based on Silver & Moore (1978) and Rachman et al. (2022). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Silver, E.A. & Moore, J.C. (1978) J. Geophys. Res. 83(B4): 1681–1691; McCaffrey, R., Silver, E.A. & Raitt, R.W. (1980) Geophys. Monogr. 23: 161; Zhang, Q. et al. (2017) JGR Solid Earth 122(5): 3977–3998.
properties.evidence_description: Inverted U-shaped seismicity Benioff zones dipping both westward and eastward beneath Sangihe and Halmahera, combined with thick central melange and ophiolitic crust exposed on Mayu, Tifore, and the Talaud Islands.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides the definitive modern analog for ancient arc-arc collision sutures preserved in orogenic belts worldwide.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the complete closure of an oceanic basin in real-time, illustrating how continental crust grows through tectonic accretion and arc collision.

properties.name: Sangihe Volcanic Arc Front Axis

properties.description: The Sangihe Volcanic Arc forms the active western volcanic chain of the Molucca Sea collision system. It extends ~500 km from the volcanic centers of North Sulawesi (Lokon, Mahawu, Soputan) northward across the Sangihe archipelago (including highly active stratovolcanoes Ruang, Karangetang, and Awu) towards Mindanao.
properties.discovery_locality: Minahasa volcanic highland to Sangihe-Talaud archipelago
properties.geometry_note: Representative LineString connecting primary active volcanic centers along the Sangihe arc volcanic front (Lokon, Ruang, Karangetang, Awu) to Mindanao border, based on PVMBG active volcano catalogs and Morrice et al. (1983). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Morrice, M.G. et al. (1983) 'An open-ocean arc-continent collision: Sangihe and Halmahera arcs, eastern Indonesia', Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research, 19(1-2): 135–165; Macpherson, C.G. & Hall, R. (2002) Chem. Geol.
properties.evidence_description: Continuous chain of active calc-alkaline to high-K stratovolcanoes and subaerial volcanic islands with deep Wadati-Benioff seismic zone dipping west to depths >600 km.
properties.evidence_significance: Key volcanic arc system recording subduction-driven magma generation and volcanic hazard evolution in Northern Indonesia.
properties.why_it_matters: Hosts several of Indonesia's most frequently active hazardous volcanoes (e.g., Karangetang and Ruang) with direct tsunami and ashfall risks to coastal island populations.
properties.source_citation: Morrice, M.G. et al. (1983) J. Volcanol. Geotherm. Res. 19(1-2): 135–165.

properties.name: Halmahera Volcanic Arc Front Axis
properties.geological_process: Eastward subduction of the Molucca Sea Plate beneath the western margin of the Halmahera microplate (Philippine Sea Plate).
properties.description: The Halmahera Volcanic Arc constitutes the eastern active volcanic arc of the Molucca Sea collision zone. It forms a distinct ~250 km chain of volcanic islands and volcanic cones along the western arm of Halmahera Island, featuring prominent active centers such as Gamalama (Ternate), Tidore, Makian, Ibu, and Dukono.
properties.discovery_locality: Western Halmahera volcanic alignment (Ternate, Tidore, Ibu, Dukono)
properties.geometry_note: Representative LineString connecting the active Quaternary volcanic vents along western Halmahera from Makian to Dukono based on Hakim & Hall (1991), Macpherson & Hall (2002), and PVMBG records. Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Hall, R., Audley-Charles, M.G., Banner, F.T., Hidayat, S. & Tobing, S.L. (1988) 'Late Palaeogene–Quaternary geology of Halmahera, Eastern Indonesia: initiation of a volcanic island arc', Journal of the Geological Society, 145(5): 829–844.
properties.evidence_description: Active basaltic-andesite to dacitic stratovolcanoes and caldera islands with an eastward-dipping seismic Wadati-Benioff zone reaching depths of ~200-250 km.
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates the young, active eastern branch of the Molucca Sea collision zone and illustrates rapid arc magmatism development in island setting.
properties.why_it_matters: Active explosive volcanoes (Ibu, Dukono, Gamalama) require continuous hazard monitoring for North Maluku's provincial population centers and air routes.
properties.source_citation: Hall, R. et al. (1988) Journal of the Geological Society, 145(5): 829–844.

properties.name: Banggai-Sula Microcontinent Platform
properties.geological_process: Continental rifting from northern Australian Gondwana margin in Mesozoic, westward strike-slip translation via Sorong Fault, and subsequent collision with East Sulawesi in Middle Miocene.
properties.description: The Banggai-Sula Microcontinent is an allochthonous continental fragment detached from the Australian passive margin in the Late Jurassic-Cretaceous. It was transported westward along the Sorong Fault system and collided with East Sulawesi during the Middle Miocene to Early Pliocene (~15-5 Ma), causing the major obduction of the East Sulawesi Ophiolite.
properties.discovery_locality: Banggai Islands, Peleng, Sula Islands (Taliabu, Mangole, Sanana)
properties.geometry_note: Representative terrane boundary polygon enclosing the Peleng, Banggai, Taliabu, Mangole, and Sanana continental platform, based on ESDM Marine Geological Institute surveys (Usman & Panuju 2013) and Garrard et al. (IPA 1988). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Silver, E.A. et al. (1985) 'Origin of the Banggai-Sula microcontinent, eastern Indonesia', Geology, 13(4): 246–249; Garrard, R.A. et al. (1988) Proc. IPA 17th Ann. Conv.
properties.evidence_description: Paleozoic granitic-metamorphic continental basement unconformably overlain by Mesozoic continental-to-marine strata and Tertiary platform carbonates.
properties.evidence_significance: Crucial evidence for continental collision mechanics and the origin of exotic terranes in the complex tectonic junction of Eastern Indonesia.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides key geological framework for petroleum exploration in the Banggai Basin and understanding Sulawesi's mountainous structural evolution.
properties.source_citation: Silver, E.A. et al. (1985) Geology, 13(4): 246–249.

properties.name: Cyclops Mountains Obducted Ophiolite Complex
properties.geological_process: Supra-subduction zone ophiolite obduction onto the northern Australian continental margin during early Miocene arc-continent collision, followed by rapid morphotectonic uplift.
properties.description: The Cyclops Mountains (Pegunungan Cyclops) on the northern coast of Papua near Jayapura expose a complete, well-preserved ophiolite sequence comprising mantle harzburgites, dunites, serpentinites, isotropic/layered gabbros, and basaltic lavas obducted during the collision of the Pacific/Caroline intra-oceanic island arc with northern New Guinea.
properties.discovery_locality: Pegunungan Cyclops Massif, north of Lake Sentani, Jayapura
properties.geometry_note: Representative boundary polygon outlining the steep Cyclops mountain massif and ophiolite outcrop north of Lake Sentani based on Monnier et al. (1999) and Salahuddin et al. (2018). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Monnier, C. et al. (1999) 'The Cyclops ophiolite (Irian Jaya, Indonesia): a fragment of early Tertiary oceanic lithosphere', Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology, 137: 249–266; Pieters, P.E. et al. (1983).
properties.evidence_description: Exposed sequence of ultramafic peridotites, pyroxenites, layered gabbros, and amphibolites with high-grade metamorphic sole rock at base of obduction thrust.
properties.evidence_significance: Documents the major Cenozoic arc-continent accretionary event that shaped the northern margin of the New Guinea landmass.
properties.why_it_matters: Forms a critical environmental watershed for the Jayapura-Sentani metropolitan basin while presenting steep landslide and debris-flow hazards during torrential rains.
properties.source_citation: Monnier, C. et al. (1999) Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology, 137: 249–266.

properties.name: Palu-Koro Left-Lateral Strike-Slip Fault
properties.geological_process: Left-lateral strike-slip faulting accommodating rapid block rotation and northward tectonic extrusion of Central/North Sulawesi relative to the Sunda block.
properties.description: The Palu-Koro Fault is one of the most active and rapidly moving strike-slip faults in Southeast Asia, with a slip rate of ~35-45 mm/year. It cuts directly through the Palu Valley and Palu Bay into central Sulawesi. On 28 September 2018, it ruptured in a catastrophic Mw 7.5 supershear earthquake, triggering devastating tsunamis and severe soil liquefaction.
properties.discovery_locality: Palu Bay, Palu Valley, Kulawi Valley to Lake Poso intersection
properties.geometry_note: Representative LineString tracing the active Palu-Koro fault trace through Palu Bay and the intermontane pull-apart valley, based on PuSGeN / ESDM Active Fault Map (2017) and Bao et al. (Nature Geoscience 2019). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Socquet, A. et al. (2006) J. Geophys. Res. 111(B8): B08409; Bao, H. et al. (2019) Nature Geoscience, 12: 200–205; Bellier, O. et al. (2001) GRL 28(2): 349–352.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent geomorphic fault scarps, offset river channels, linear pull-apart graben valley, and well-documented 2018 surface rupture offsets exceeding 5 meters.
properties.evidence_significance: A globally benchmarked strike-slip fault illustrating persistent supershear earthquake rupture dynamics, submarine landsliding, and major soil liquefaction.
properties.why_it_matters: Direct seismic and geohazard threat to Palu City and Central Sulawesi; cross-referenced with historical hazard event haz_palu_2018.
properties.source_citation: Socquet, A. et al. (2006) J. Geophys. Res. 111(B8): B08409; Bao, H. et al. (2019) Nature Geoscience, 12: 200–205.

properties.name: Nanggulan Formation Eocene Marine Fossil Beds
properties.geological_age: Middle Eocene to Late Oligocene (~45 - 28 Ma)
properties.geological_process: Transgressive Coastal to Shallow-Marine Clastic Sedimentation
properties.description: The basal Eocene marine sedimentary unit of the Kulon Progo Mountains dome sequence, famously exposed along Kali Songgo and Kalipururu. Contains one of Southeast Asia's most exceptionally preserved and diverse Eocene molluscan faunas and index foraminifera, forming the foundational stratigraphic base overlain by the Old Andesite Formation and younger Miocene Jonggrangan and Sentolo carbonates.
properties.discovery_locality: Kali Songgo & Kalipururu, Nanggulan / Kalibawang, Kulon Progo, DIY
properties.fossil_material: Larger foraminifera (Nummulites, Discocyclina), diverse mollusks (Turritella, Conus, Voluta, Cardita, Nucula), solitary corals (Trochocyathus), decapod crabs
properties.paleoenvironment: Tropical shallow-marine littoral to inner-shelf embayment
properties.geometry_note: Point precisely anchored to the classic Kali Songgo type section near Watupuru/Kembang in Nanggulan, Kulon Progo, based on P3G/Badan Geologi sheet mapping and paleontological type literature.
properties.source: Woodhouse, A. et al. (2025) J. Micropalaeontology 44: 601–632; Martin, K. (1914–1915) Die Fauna des Obereocäns von Nanggulan auf Java; Purnamaningsih, S. & Pringgoprawiro, H. (1981) GRDC Paleont. Ser. 1: 9–28.
properties.evidence_description: Pristinely preserved aragonitic mollusk shells, larger foraminifera tests, and solitary corals weathering out of quartz sandstones and lignite-bearing silty claystones along river banks.
properties.evidence_significance: International paleontological benchmark for Eocene-Oligocene macro-invertebrate and foraminiferal biostratigraphy across the Indo-Pacific realm.
properties.why_it_matters: Represents the oldest sedimentary basement of the Kulon Progo dome; demonstrates initial Cenozoic marine transgression across Sundaland before major volcanic arc development.
properties.source_citation: Woodhouse, A. et al. (2025) J. Micropalaeontology 44: 601–632; Martin, K. (1914–1915) Samml. Geol. Reichs-Mus. Leiden.

properties.name: Baturaja Formation Miocene Carbonate Reef Beds
properties.geological_process: Tropical Shallow-Water Carbonate Platform & Pinnacle Reef Development
properties.description: Extensive Early-Middle Miocene platform carbonate and coral reef complex in the South Sumatra Basin, prominently cropping out around Baturaja, Bukit Telunjuk, and Gua Putri. Highly fossiliferous limestone sequence containing abundant larger benthic foraminifera, colonial corals, bryozoans, and mollusks, serving as Indonesia's classic reference for Cenozoic carbonate reservoir geology.
properties.discovery_locality: Baturaja Quarry Belt & Gua Putri / Padang Bindu, Ogan Komering Ulu, South Sumatra
properties.fossil_material: Larger benthic foraminifera (Lepidocyclina, Miogypsina, Spiroclypeus), hermatypic corals (Porites, Favites, Acropora), coralline red algae (Lithothamnium), bryozoans, mollusks
properties.paleoenvironment: Tropical shallow-water carbonate platform, reef crest, and lagoonal shelf
properties.geometry_note: Point anchored to the primary Baturaja type outcrop and karst quarry area in Ogan Komering Ulu, based on Gafoer et al. (1993) P3G/Badan Geologi mapping.
properties.source: Barber, A.J., Crow, M.J. & Milsom, J.S. (2005) Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution, Geol. Soc. Lond. Mem. 31; Pulunggono, A. et al. (1992) Proc. Indon. Petrol. Assoc. 21st Ann. Conv.
properties.evidence_description: Massive skeletal packstones, boundstones, and wackestones rich in larger foraminiferal tests, branching coral colonies, and coralline algal crusts forming distinctive karst topography.
properties.evidence_significance: Key biostratigraphic marker for the Early Miocene marine transgressive climax across the back-arc basins of western Indonesia.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides crucial paleoclimate and paleoecological records of the Miocene Climatic Optimum and forms the primary productive carbonate reservoir rock in South Sumatra.
properties.source_citation: Barber, A.J., Crow, M.J. & Milsom, J.S. (2005) Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution, Geol. Soc. Lond. Mem. 31.

properties.name: Karangbolong Coastal Reef Carbonate Formation
properties.geological_age: Late Oligocene to Middle Miocene (~24 - 12 Ma)
properties.geological_process: Coastal Carbonate Reef Accretion & Volcaniclastic Interbedding
properties.description: Spectacular karstified coastal limestone and volcaniclastic succession in the Karangbolong Mountains of southern Kebumen. Forms steep marine cliffs and caves rich in larger benthic foraminifera, coral heads, and coralline algae, situated immediately south of the Karangsambung accretionary complex and recording Neogene island-arc shallow-marine sedimentation.
properties.discovery_locality: Karangbolong Mountain Range, Buayan / Ayah, Kebumen, Central Java
properties.fossil_material: Larger benthic foraminifera (Lepidocyclina, Miogypsina, Cycloclypeus, Amphistegina), massive reef-building corals, red coralline algae, molluscan shell beds
properties.paleoenvironment: High-energy coastal reef barrier and shallow carbonate shelf
properties.geometry_note: Point located at the primary Karangbolong limestone cliff and karst ridge in southern Kebumen, based on Asikin et al. (1992) P3G/Badan Geologi geological mapping.
properties.source: Haryono, E., Suratman, & Putro, S.T. (2017) 'Karst Morphology of Karangbolong Area, Java-Indonesia', Acta Carsologica, 46(1): 17–28; Hantoro, W.S. (2021) J. Geol. Sumberdaya Mineral, 22(2).
properties.evidence_description: Well-bedded to massive bioclast-rich limestones and reefal floatstones exposed along sea cliffs and karst towers containing dense concentrations of discoidal foraminifera and coral fragments.
properties.evidence_significance: Documents the transition from Paleogene deep-subduction mélangé (Karangsambung) to Neogene shallow-water arc carbonate deposition in Central Java.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides key structural and paleontological links between Java's subduction basement and overlying Neogene volcanic-carbonate cover sequences.
properties.source_citation: Haryono, E. et al. (2017) 'Karst Morphology of Karangbolong Area, Java-Indonesia', Acta Carsologica, 46(1): 17–28.

properties.name: Rajamandala Formation Oligo-Miocene Coral & Foram Reef
properties.geological_age: Late Oligocene to Early Miocene (~28 - 20 Ma)
properties.geological_process: Barrier Reef & Carbonate Platform Accretion along Active Basin Margin
properties.description: A prominent ~50 km long limestone karst ridge extending from Padalarang (Gunung Masigit, Guha Pawon) to Sukabumi in West Java. Represents a world-renowned Oligo-Miocene barrier reef complex densely populated by giant larger foraminifera (Lepidocyclina eulepidina, Spiroclypeus), branching and head corals, rhodoliths, and calcareous algae.
properties.discovery_locality: Gunung Masigit & Gunung Pawon Ridge, Padalarang, West Bandung, West Java
properties.fossil_material: Giant larger foraminifera (Eulepidina dilatata, Nephrolepidina, Spiroclypeus, Miogypsinoides), colonial corals (Favites, Goniopora, Porites), coralline red algae (Lithoporella), mollusks
properties.paleoenvironment: High-energy barrier reef tract, forereef talus, and back-reef carbonate platform
properties.geometry_note: Point precisely positioned on the type reef limestone ridge at Gunung Masigit / Guha Pawon, Padalarang, based on Sudjatmiko (2003) Badan Geologi mapping and UNPAD stratigraphic research.
properties.source: Maryunani, K.A. et al. (2012) 'Biostratigraphy and depositional environment of the Rajamandala Formation, West Java', Indonesian Journal on Geoscience, 4(3): 203–213; Baumann, P. (1972) Proc. IPA 1st Ann. Conv.
properties.evidence_description: Tower karst cliffs composed of recrystallized boundstones and grainstones densely packed with coin-sized Lepidocyclina tests and preserved coral frameworks.
properties.evidence_significance: The definitive stratotype for Late Oligocene to Early Miocene (Letter Stage Te1-4) larger foraminiferal zonation in Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Exemplifies classic tropical reef development in an active volcanic-tectonic basin; prominent geoheritage site and vital source of paleotectonic data for western Java.
properties.source_citation: Maryunani, K.A. et al. (2012) Indonesian Journal on Geoscience, 4(3): 203–213.

properties.name: Jonggrangan Formation Miocene Carbonate Platform
properties.geological_process: Bioherm Reef & Carbonate Platform Capping Volcanic Dome
properties.description: The middle carbonate unit of the Kulon Progo Mountains stratigraphic dome sequence, directly overlying the eroded volcanic core of the Old Andesite Formation (OAF) in the central highlands (Jonggrangan plateau, Goa Kiskendo). Rich in massive reef corals, larger foraminifera, and mollusks, representing shallow-water carbonate platform growth while deeper marls of the coeval Sentolo Formation accumulated on the eastern flanks.
properties.discovery_locality: Jonggrangan Plateau & Goa Kiskendo, Girimulyo / Kokap, Kulon Progo, DIY
properties.fossil_material: Biohermal corals (Porites, Acropora), larger foraminifera (Lepidocyclina, Miogypsina, Cycloclypeus, Marginopora), red algae (Lithothamnium), molluscan casts, echinoids
properties.paleoenvironment: Tropical shallow-water reef crest, bioherm buildup, and plateau platform
properties.geometry_note: Point located at the type Jonggrangan limestone plateau near Goa Kiskendo in Girimulyo, Kulon Progo, based on Rahardjo et al. (1995) P3G/Badan Geologi mapping.
properties.source: Husein, S. et al. (2019) 'Fasies Terumbu Batugamping Formasi Jonggrangan di Daerah Kulon Progo', Riset Geologi dan Pertambangan, 29(1): 1–14; Pringgoprawiro, H. & Sukido (1983) Peta Geologi Lembar Yogyakarta.
properties.evidence_description: Massive reefal limestones, calcarenites, and bedded biomicrites forming high karst plateaus and cave systems with abundant embedded coral molds and foraminifera.
properties.evidence_significance: Crucial member of the tripartite Kulon Progo succession (Nanggulan -> Jonggrangan -> Sentolo), documenting early Middle Miocene volcanic quiescence and shallow-sea carbonate colonization.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how tropical coral reef platforms colonize extinct volcanic island edifices, forming spectacular cave karst landscapes in Java.
properties.source_citation: Husein, S. et al. (2019) Riset Geologi dan Pertambangan, 29(1): 1–14.

properties.name: Sentolo Formation Mio-Pliocene Foraminiferal Marl Beds
properties.geological_age: Middle Miocene to Early Pliocene (~15 - 4 Ma)
properties.geological_process: Open-Marine Shelf, Slope, and Basinal Pelagic-Calcareous Deposition
properties.description: The youngest marine sedimentary formation of the Kulon Progo Mountains dome sequence, forming the eastern and southern flanks along Sentolo and Kali Pengasih. Interfingers with and stratigraphically succeeds the Jonggrangan reef complex, consisting of tuffaceous marls, bedded calcarenites, and calcareous sandstones packed with continuous planktic foraminifera biozones and calcareous nannofossils.
properties.taxon_name: Globigerinoides / Globorotalia menardii / Orbulina universa / Amphistegina
properties.discovery_locality: Kali Pengasih & Sentolo Hills along Progo River, Sentolo, Kulon Progo, DIY
properties.fossil_material: Abundant planktic foraminifera (Globorotalia menardii, Globigerinoides, Orbulina universa, Neogloboquadrina), benthic foraminifera (Amphistegina, Bolivina, Uvigerina), calcareous nannoplankton
properties.paleoenvironment: Open-marine outer neritic to upper bathyal shelf and slope
properties.geometry_note: Point positioned along Kali Pengasih and the Sentolo type outcrop area in eastern Kulon Progo, based on Rahardjo et al. (1995) P3G/Badan Geologi mapping and Pringgoprawiro (1985).
properties.source: Subandrio, A. et al. (2022) 'Biostratigrafi Foraminifera Plangtonik dan Lingkungan Pengendapan Formasi Sentolo', Jurnal Geologi dan Sumberdaya Mineral, 23(3): 143–154; Kadar, D. (1986) GRDC Spec. Publ. 5.
properties.evidence_description: Thick sequence of yellowish-white stratified marls and calcarenites yielding dense microfossil assemblages of planktic and benthic foraminifera tests.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides an unbroken high-resolution biochronological record spanning Middle Miocene to Early Pliocene (N9 to N19/N20) across Central Java.
properties.why_it_matters: Completes the classical Kulon Progo Cenozoic sedimentary dome cycle (Nanggulan -> Jonggrangan -> Sentolo), documenting the gradual regional drowning and basin-margin sedimentation.
properties.source_citation: Subandrio, A. et al. (2022) Jurnal Geologi dan Sumberdaya Mineral, 23(3): 143–154.

properties.name: Cibodas Formation Miocene Carbonate Shelf Outcrop
properties.description: Middle to Late Miocene marine carbonate and clastic formation exposed in the Jampang / Ciracap sector of southern Sukabumi. Contains fossiliferous limestone lenses bearing larger benthic foraminifera, red algae, and molluscan bioclasts deposited in a shallow shelf setting.
properties.discovery_locality: Ciracap & Cibodas area, Ciemas / Surade, Sukabumi, West Java
properties.fossil_material: Larger benthic foraminifera (Lepidocyclina, Cycloclypeus, Amphistegina), molluscan bioclasts, coralline red algae fragments
properties.paleoenvironment: Shallow marine continental shelf with localized carbonate buildups
properties.geometry_note: Representative point for the Ciracap-Cibodas limestone outcrop sector based on Sukamto (1975) Jampang sheet mapping and UNPAD geological field surveys; exact type section boundary retains spatial variance.
properties.source: Silalahi, N.N., Pratiwi, S.D. & Patonah, A. (2025) 'Studi Batugamping Berdasarkan Kandungan Foraminifera Besar di Daerah Ciracap, Sukabumi', Bulletin of Scientific Contribution, 23(1); Winarto, J.B. (2022) JGSM.
properties.evidence_description: Bedded calcarenites, sandy limestones, and bioclast-rich marls containing larger foraminiferal tests and fragmented marine shells.
properties.evidence_significance: Documents Middle-Late Miocene shallow-marine carbonate sedimentation in the Southern Mountains of West Java.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides insights into post-volcanic shelf evolution in southern Sukabumi; maintained in Candidate/Review pending detailed type-section delineation.
properties.source_citation: Silalahi, N.N. et al. (2025) Bulletin of Scientific Contribution, 23(1).

properties.name: Gumai Formation Marine Transgressive Microfossil Beds
properties.geological_process: Regional Maximum Marine Transgression Deep-Shale Sedimentation
properties.description: The principal deep-marine shale and marl formation of the South Sumatra Basin, deposited during the maximum regional marine transgression (Early to Middle Miocene). Locally exposed along river valleys near Muaradua in OKU Selatan, yielding rich planktic and bathyal benthic foraminiferal microfossil assemblages.
properties.taxon_name: Globigerinoides sicanus / Praeorbulina glomerosa / Globorotalia peripheroronda
properties.discovery_locality: Komering River Section, Muaradua, Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan, South Sumatra
properties.fossil_material: Planktic foraminifera index microfossils (Globigerinoides sicanus, Praeorbulina, Globorotalia), deep-shelf to bathyal benthic foraminifera (Bathysiphon, Cyclammina), micro-mollusks
properties.paleoenvironment: Outer neritic to bathyal open-marine basin and deep shelf
properties.geometry_note: Representative point for the Gumai shale river-cut exposures in the Muaradua area based on Gafoer et al. (1993) mapping; regional shale distribution is widespread across South Sumatra.
properties.source: Barber, A.J., Crow, M.J. & Milsom, J.S. (2005) Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution, Geol. Soc. Lond. Mem. 31; Pulunggono, A. et al. (1992) Proc. IPA 21st Ann. Conv.
properties.evidence_description: Dark grey to black fossiliferous calcareous shales and marls with abundant microscopic planktic foraminifera tests.
properties.evidence_significance: Defines the peak Cenozoic marine inundation and regional seal rock across the South Sumatra hydrocarbon province.
properties.why_it_matters: Crucial regional microfossil marker for petroleum source and seal rock studies; maintained in Candidate/Review due to diffuse regional outcrop extent.
properties.source_citation: Barber, A.J., Crow, M.J. & Milsom, J.S. (2005) Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution, Geol. Soc. Lond. Mem. 31.
